query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: The core target variable for this query. Derivable from opened_at/closed_at timestamps present in the table. Note the samples show resolution_hours=24.0 despite opened_at not appearing and closed==updated, but the value is a warranted computation from available timestamp columns; NULLs for open incidents are correct.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Aggregate of per-incident resolution_hours grouped by assigned_to, a genuine new axis to compare performers. Fully derivable from table-internal columns.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Category-level average of resolution time; supports identifying slow categories to target. Derived from category + resolution_hours in-table.

per_column.name: resolution_vs_assignee_avg
per_column.rationale: Deviation of an incident from its assignee's average — useful for spotting outlier cases, though it is a straightforward arithmetic combination of two other added columns. Still adds a comparative lens. Grounded in derived values.

per_column.name: priority_urgency_score
per_column.rationale: A numeric encoding of the existing priority column, so largely redundant with an original field; mild usefulness for modeling. Values plausibly map from priority but the encoding scheme is opaque and only weakly evidenced in samples.

per_column.name: no_handoff
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for whether the incident stayed with one owner is a genuinely relevant driver of resolution time. Plausibly derivable from assigned_to vs closed_by/assignment_group, though the exact basis is not directly visible in the samples, lowering groundedness somewhat.

judge.rationale: The added columns are well-targeted to reducing resolution time: they construct the target metric (resolution_hours) and provide multiple genuine grouping/comparison axes (per-assignee, per-category, deviation, handoff). Most values are soundly derivable from in-table timestamp, assignment, and category fields, with correct NULLs for unresolved rows. priority_urgency_score is the weakest, being a near-restatement of the existing priority column, and no_handoff's derivation basis is only inferable. No hallucinated facts observed.
